question: A 2013 genome scan linked nearly 200 genes to convergence between echolocating bats and dolphins. What did later control comparisons find?
options: As much convergence in non-echolocating pairs
answer: As much convergence in non-echolocating pairs. Thomas and Hahn, and separately Zou and Zhang, ran the same test on mammals with no sonar in common and found as many shared changes or more; across thousands of genes, chance and shared constraints throw up matches. What survives is narrower, such as the hearing protein prestin.
move: Search enough places and matches appear; ask how many chance alone would give.
ask: When I find a pattern, have I asked how often chance alone would produce the same match?
trap: Trusting hits from a scan of thousands of genes without a baseline.
source: Thomas & Hahn, Molecular Biology and Evolution, 2015
reference: Thomas & Hahn, Determining the null model for detecting adaptive convergence from genomic data: a case study using echolocating mammals, Molecular Biology and Evolution, 2015; Parker et al., Genome-wide signatures of convergent evolution in echolocating mammals, Nature, 2013
